- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (especially > -1.0 in change), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.0+), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is stable or mildly positive (0.33–0.67) and news volume is high, model underestimates upward momentum — add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., < 0.33) and news volume is steady, model tends to underestimate downside — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for hidden volatility.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts by 1–3 days — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.2–0.7% for positive sentiment shifts, -0.2–0.5% for negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates near-term volatility — cap forecast deviation at ±1.0% from 14-day moving average to avoid overreaction.
